opportunities.title: Harmony Gets Hacked Again: Why 'Rollback or Rugpull' Was Always the Only Choice
opportunities.why_now: Harmony just confirmed a 4B ONE token mint exploit and is weighing a rollback, replaying its 2022 Horizon Bridge playbook almost beat for beat.
opportunities.angle: Timeline comparison piece: 2022 bridge hack vs. 2026 mint exploit, arguing chains that never fix root causes just wait for the next incident — end with what 'rollback' really signals to holders.

opportunities.title: Your Coldcard Wasn't the Weak Link — Your Habits Were
opportunities.why_now: Fresh reporting on how investigators are tracing Coldcard-hack proceeds gives a rare inside look at post-theft forensics most holders never see.
opportunities.angle: Explainer using the trace methodology as a teaching moment on wallet hygiene (address reuse, seed backup exposure) — position as the 'autopsy' piece for self-custody users.

opportunities.title: The Quantum Attack Is Already Happening — It Just Looks Like an Ordinary Hack
opportunities.why_now: A Quantus founder just warned that crypto's first quantum break will be indistinguishable from routine key theft, which is exactly the kind of slow-motion risk this channel is built to flag before consensus catches up.
opportunities.angle: Thesis piece: list recent 'unexplained' key thefts and ask which ones could already be quantum, framed as 'priced in before anyone admits it.'

opportunities.title: Ravencoin's Rollback Threat Is a Preview of Every Small Chain's Endgame
opportunities.why_now: Ravencoin just crashed 20% on a critical exploit that could force a network rollback, days after Harmony faced the same dilemma.
opportunities.angle: Comparative security note: what determines whether a chain can even attempt a rollback (miner/validator concentration), and why smaller-cap chains keep drawing these attacks.

opportunities.title: A $200K XRP Bridge Drain Over Fake Deposits Is the Oldest Bug in the Book
opportunities.why_now: An XRP bridge got drained for $200K because its software 'mistook fake deposits for real ones' — the exact deposit-verification flaw that has sunk bridges for years.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition post: catalog past bridge hacks caused by the same fake-deposit/verification gap, arguing bridges remain crypto's most 'already priced' attack surface.
